data.author: Map
data.comment: Root cause (reproduced by a 250-boot stress harness): the Centipede weave folds neighbouring segments close together at horizontal direction reversals. When the test fires a zero-velocity player bullet at segment #2's centre, a folded neighbour (#0 or #1) can lie within the overlap radius and appears earlier in the collision iteration order, so it absorbs the shot and #2 survives — e.g. victim #2 (837.8,145.4) with #0 at (839.4,154.4) (~9 px apart, overlap threshold ~21 px). The game behaviour is correct; the test assumed the target was spatially isolated. Fix: (1) disable the random asteroid spawner in bootWithCentipedeWave (a released asteroid can likewise absorb the shot), and (2) advance the weave (bounded, <= 100 x 0.05 s) until segment #2's clearance to every other enemy exceeds the bullet radius before firing. Stress-validated 0/300 boots with the fix; full suite determinism restored.
